$comment: Multi-forge registry per docs/MULTI_FORGE_ARCHITECTURE.md §3. JSON, not the YAML sketched in that doc's prose -- every other file in core/config/ is JSON and this avoids adding a PyYAML dependency for one file. canonical_forge is the single source of truth for governance (PRs/issues/collaboration); mirrors are read-only replicas, never a second place to push to.

mirrors.note: Configured 2026-09-10 on the GitLab side (Settings -> Repository -> Mirroring repositories, Pull, all branches, confirmed via GitLab UI 'Mirrored from https://github.com/yanacuti1121/Yana-AI.git'). Both the GitLab group (yana-ai-group) and this project had to be set to Public separately -- group-level Public alone did not make the project visible via GitLab's unauthenticated API, confirmed live 2026-09-10 (project returned 404 until its own Visibility setting was also changed). Verified SYNCED same day: GitLab's 'main' branch HEAD (ab19d2e8f106...) matches GitHub's live HEAD exactly. GitLab's project-info API briefly reported default_branch as an unrelated branch name during initial import -- confirmed to be an import-time quirk, not a real problem: 'main' itself was present with the correct SHA the whole time.

sync_transport.risk: GitLab's native Pull Mirroring is only available on paid tiers -- currently active under an Ultimate Trial. The architecture must not depend on this specific transport surviving past the trial.
sync_transport.fallback: github-actions-scheduled-push-mirror (design only, not built -- see docs/MULTI_FORGE_ARCHITECTURE.md §5's adapter-abstraction note). A GitHub Actions job doing `git push --mirror` on a schedule would keep the same GitHub-canonical/GitLab-replica shape without any paid GitLab feature.
sync_transport.status_check_dependency: none -- core/scripts/check_forge_sync.py only reads each forge's public REST API for its current HEAD SHA; it never talks to whichever mechanism keeps the mirror updated, so swapping 'active' for 'fallback' later requires no change to the status checker.
